strategies.summary: Identify a dual-sweep consolidation regime where price takes liquidity on both sides, returns to equilibrium, and PD arrays stop producing follow-through. Stand aside on trend-continuation ideas until a higher-timeframe displacement fair value gap breaks the range.

timeframes.notes: Use the daily or 4h chart to diagnose the range. The lesson rejects 1-minute fair value gaps as valid exits, so the breakout confirmation must come from the same higher-timeframe regime (4h or 1d).

glossary.Seek and Destroy: A dual-sided liquidity trap where price sweeps both sides of a range, returns toward equilibrium, and behaves as consolidation until a higher-timeframe displacement ends it.

custom_signals.name: consolidation
custom_signals.plain_definition: Sideways price action with no expansion over a recent window.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: highest(high, K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES) - lowest(low, K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES) <= K_CONSOLIDATION_RANGE_ATR * atr

custom_signals.name: dealing_range
custom_signals.plain_definition: A price range whose low swept the prior swing low (sell-side) and whose high swept the prior swing high (buy-side).

custom_signals.name: equilibrium_reversion
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades back to the 50% midpoint of the current dual-sweep dealing range.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.dealing_range AND low <= (swing_low[0].price + swing_high[0].price) / 2 AND high >= (swing_low[0].price + swing_high[0].price) / 2

custom_signals.name: pd_array_failure
custom_signals.plain_definition: After price returns to equilibrium, premium or discount arrays stop producing follow-through fair value gaps and price behaves as consolidation.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: any(custom_signals.equilibrium_reversion, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) AND custom_signals.consolidation AND count(fvg.formed, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) == 0

custom_signals.name: displacement_candle
custom_signals.plain_definition: A strong expansion candle in the trade direction.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: close > open AND body >= K_DISPLACEMENT_BODY_MULT * avg(body[-1], K_DISPLACEMENT_LOOKBACK)

custom_signals.name: htf_range_displacement
custom_signals.plain_definition: A higher-timeframe bullish displacement candle forms a fair value gap completely above the prior consolidation range, ending Seek and Destroy conditions.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: any(custom_signals.pd_array_failure, K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES) AND custom_signals.displacement_candle AND bullish_fvg[0].formed AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low > highest(high[-1], K_CONSOLIDATION_CANDLES)

sequence: Wait for the higher-timeframe range to sweep sell-side liquidity.
Wait for the same expansion to sweep the opposing buy-side liquidity and complete the dealing range.
Mark the 50% equilibrium of that range and wait for price to trade back into it.
Treat the environment as Seek and Destroy once equilibrium holds as consolidation and no follow-through fair value gap appears.

invalidation.text: Seek and Destroy conditions terminate when price displaces cleanly out of the consolidation range on a higher timeframe leaving an FVG, and PD arrays resume following through.

filters.text: Trend-following traders must stop trading or stay out of the market once PD arrays fail to follow through near equilibrium.
Do not consider lower-timeframe (e.g. 1-minute) fair value gaps as valid displacement out of the consolidation range; displacement must be on a higher timeframe.

entry_rule.text: No execution entry is taught here; the lesson only labels the environment and defers turtle-soup execution to the next episode.
entry_rule.quote: in the next episode I exactly want to go over Turtle soups and I want to go over how we can potentially capitalize on these conditions

target_rule.text: Price tends to refer back to the 50% equilibrium of the dual-sweep range after both sides are taken.
target_rule.quote: like a magnet price will refer back to the 50 percent of that most recent range which is that that is equilibrium

presenter_claims.claim: Consolidation at the 50% equilibrium is guaranteed once PD arrays stop following through.
Displacement out of Seek and Destroy conditions usually happens during NFP, CPI, or FOMC news releases.

strategies.notes: Conditions filter, not an entry model. The machine proxy treats the presenter's dual-sweep expansion as the current dealing range, then uses a midpoint return plus no follow-through fair value gap as the Seek-and-Destroy condition. A 1-minute gap does not end the regime; the range exit must print as a higher-timeframe displacement fair value gap.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price takes out major sell-side liquidity at the low of a consolidation.
Price immediately targets and sweeps the opposing buy-side liquidity at the highs.
Price returns to the 50% equilibrium of the expansion range.
Premium arrays (FVG and OB) fail to push price lower, leaving daily wicks without follow-through.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price takes out a major liquidity pool and refers back to 50% equilibrium.
Price enters an FVG and an order block but fails to follow through, leaving wick-heavy price action.
A new higher-timeframe FVG forms that completely displaces out of the gray consolidation range, confirming the end of Seek and Destroy conditions.

examples.presenter_commentary: He shows how to recognize the end of the consolidation. A lower-timeframe FVG is not enough; you need a higher-timeframe displacement (usually news-driven like NFP/CPI) completely clearing the consolidation area.

may_differ.reason: Traidle would detect the structural FVG, but requires a custom module to evaluate its position strictly relative to a drawn consolidation box.
